content: A classification model is trained to predict the primary diagnosis given the content of the cancer pathology report. The performance results on this task are reported in tab:results. We can observe that the XGBoost classifier outperformed all other models for both the micro F-score metric, with a score of 0.92, and the macro F-score metric, with a score of 0.31. This was an improvement of 7% for the micro F-score over the next best model, SVM-L, and a marginal improvement of 5% for macro F-score. It is interesting to note that SVM with linear kernels performs much better than SVM with RBF kernel, scoring 9% on the macro F-score and 12% more on the micro F-score. It is suspected that since words used in primary diagnosis itself occur in some reports, thus enabling the linear models to outperform complex models.
